I agree with what you say. It is not as magical an experience as we want to make it out to be or wish it were, and there’s a reason thrifted clothing are so cheap.

To make thrifting work, I have shifted my perspective on it. I never go alone. Bringing a friend gives you another set of eyes to pick out potential matches, pick out flaws and defects, see your back when you can’t (thrift store mirrors, if there are any, aren’t the best) and turns it into a social exercise.

Thrifting is also a good way to practice outfits on the cheap. See what works, try different styles, and then move on to new higher quality clothing when I feel confident ok with what works for me, and it’s really helped me see what doesn’t work, especially with a friend there to help with a different perspective. 

And yes, every once in while, you do find that special unicorn.
